RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Riley Kimura

Reference Number: POC-F4D8086686-78032
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-11
Requested Service: Rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827
Treating Surgeon: [Reyes, MD — practice name, address, phone, fax, NPI not provided in records]

To the Complaint and Appeals Coordinator:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29827 (arthroscopic rotator cuff repair) referenced above. The notice of adverse benefit determination states that the denial reason is that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I disagree with this determination and ask that it be reversed on the basis of the clinical record summarized below.

Preliminary note on the applicable policy: The denial notice states that this determination was made under "the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria," but it does not name, number, date, or quote that policy, and I have not been able to obtain a copy of it. I am not able to quote or cite the specific plan document because it was not provided to me, and I am not attaching any purported quotation from it. I formally request, as part of this appeal, that Avera Health Plans provide me and my surgeon's office with the specific medical policy, clinical criteria, and any internal or licensed guideline (for example, InterQual or MCG, if used) that was applied to reach this denial, including the policy title, policy number, and effective date, so that I may respond to it directly. Please treat this as a request for the diagnostic and rationale documents under the plan's claims and appeals disclosure obligations.

In the absence of the specific policy language, I address the stated reason for denial — that the imaging findings do not support medical necessity — using the clinical findings actually in the prior authorization packet:

1. Duration and nature of symptoms: I have had 24 months of progressive shoulder pain that has not been relieved by rest.

2. Imaging findings: MRI of the shoulder performed 2026-07-11 shows a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm, with grade 2 fatty atrophy. This is a structural, imaging-confirmed rotator cuff tear, not merely a clinical impression.

3. Exam findings: Physical examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain, which corroborates the imaging findings and correlates the tear with my reported symptoms.

4. Functional limitation: I am unable to lift my arm above shoulder height and cannot sleep on the affected side, both of which reflect significant functional impairment from this injury.

5. Conservative treatment already completed:
   - Supervised physical therapy focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, 12 weeks, from 2026-04-10 to 2026-07-03, with 16 visits completed, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
   - NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief.
   - Corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-22, which provided only 4 weeks of partial relief.

6. Absence of contraindications: I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker, none of which should present a barrier to surgical repair.

Taken together, this record shows an imaging-confirmed, full-thickness rotator cuff tear that correlates with positive exam findings and significant functional loss, in a patient who has completed a substantial, well-documented course of conservative care (structured physical therapy, prolonged NSAID use, and corticosteroid injection) without durable relief. I am not aware of what specific imaging or documentation element the plan's reviewer found insufficient, since the denial notice does not identify which criterion was unmet. I therefore also request, as part of this appeal, a written explanation identifying the specific criterion or element within the applicable medical policy that the reviewer determined was not satisfied by the submitted MRI and clinical records, so that my surgeon and I can respond to that specific point if any further clarification is needed.

My surgeon, Dr. Reyes, is available for a peer-to-peer discussion with the plan's medical reviewer and can provide any additional clarifying documentation the plan requires. Please contact [surgeon's office phone/fax not provided in records] to arrange this.

I understand that this appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the denial notice, i.e., by 2027-02-07, and I am submitting this appeal well within that window. I request a written determination on this appeal as required under the plan's appeal procedures, and I ask to be notified of that determination, along with any further appeal or external review rights, in writing at the address above.

Enclosed with this letter are copies of:
- The MRI report dated 2026-07-11
- The physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-10 through 2026-07-03)
- Documentation of the corticosteroid injection dated 2026-04-22
- Clinic notes reflecting exam findings and functional limitations
- [Any additional surgeon's letter of medical necessity, if available]

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide the name and direct contact information of the person handling my case.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Riley Kimura
